subject: AcadiaHealth deployment follow-up — sizing clarifications & next steps
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Gomez <marta.gomez@acadiahealth.com>, Sam Lee <sam.lee@acadiahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 23 Jan 2027 14:30:00 -0800
Subject: AcadiaHealth deployment follow-up — sizing clarifications & next steps

Hi Marta / Sam —

Thanks again for the call earlier — great context on the triage and intake use cases. I wanted to capture a concise recap and the minimal items we need to size a dedicated pool that meets your latency & throughput goals. Below are the assumptions from our discussion and a short ask list so we can produce a concrete capacity proposal by EOD Monday.

Recap (what you told us)
- Primary workload: clinical triage chat + form summarization. Typical session = 1 prompt + 2 follow-ups, average generation ~ 120 tokens.
- Peak TPS target (user-facing inference calls): 40 TPS sustained for 10 minute bursts, 120 TPS short spikes (<=90s).
- Desired p95 latency: <= 450ms for single-turn generation (50 tokens gen).
- Data residency: must run in your VPC (private deployment) OR Redwood Dedicated in the us-west region with a contractually isolated pool — procurement leaning towards Dedicated for now.

Sizing assumptions we plan to validate
- Token mix: 30% long-context (1k+ prompt tokens), 70% short prompts; please confirm sample distribution.
- Concurrency model: we assume many short-lived sessions (chatty) => high concurrency with small per-request generation.
- Model family preference: you mentioned preferring an H100-backed instance for latency headroom. We'll size for both H100 and A100 profiles to show cost/latency tradeoffs.

Asks (attachments included)
1) Please drop a 48-hour sample of production-style traffic (or synthetic sample) — attached acadia_token_samples.csv is an example template. We need per-request: timestamp, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, model_variant_preference (if any).
2) Confirm whether any long-running streaming sessions (multi-minute writes) exist.
3) Confirm strict p95 latency target and whether 99th percentile SLO should be included in the proposal.
4) Point person for procurement to receive the Dedicated contract stub — we’ll include burst credits and SLA options.

Deliverable plan
- Monday: Dedicated capacity worksheet (H100 vs A100 variants) + estimated monthly commit and suggested canary plan.
- Tuesday: if you opt for Dedicated, we’ll schedule an ops walkthrough for networking/VPC peering (1 hr).

Attachments: acadia_token_samples.csv, acadia_capacity_workbook.xlsx

Thanks — I’ll loop Ben & Priyom on sizing details.

Best,
Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0112

---
Note: If you prefer Private VPC/on-prem, we can swap the worksheet to a VPC network checklist and HSM/KMS carrier options; that will change lead times for procurement.

From: Marta Gomez <marta.gomez@acadiahealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 23 Jan 2027 14:55:22 -0800
Subject: Re: AcadiaHealth deployment follow-up — sizing clarifications & next steps

Thanks, Olga — very helpful summary. A few quick clarifications: 

- Token sample: I’ll export 72 hours of anonymized traffic and map into the CSV template by Monday morning. Expect a mix skewed toward short sessions; we do have a smaller set (maybe 8% of calls) that are long context (1.5k–3k tokens) for case history retrieval.
- TPS: the 40 TPS sustained is our conservative plan for business hours across the East / West regions. The 120 TPS spike is a firm upper bound for incident surges.
- Latency SLO: aiming for p95 <= 350ms if possible, but we can accept 450ms as a contingency for heavy context requests. Please show both in the workbook.
- Model: We have a preference for an H100-backed option for production, but we’d like to see A100 cost delta for a canary pool.

Procurement: copying procurement@acadiahealth.com and Sam (internal infra) — they’ll confirm contract channel. We’re open to Dedicated as the first step; Private VPC is preferred for later-stage compliance gating.

Thanks — I’ll send the token sample + a short spreadsheet with session tags Monday AM.

—Marta
Marta Gomez
Director, Digital Ops | AcadiaHealth
marta.gomez@acadiahealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 23 Jan 2027 15:10:05 -0800
Subject: RE: AcadiaHealth — quick sizing notes

Olga / Priyom — thanks for the heads-up. A few internal notes before we finalize the workbook: 

- GPU choice: H100 gives us ~1.5–2x inference speed for the 70–1k token range vs A100 (model dependent). For p95<=350ms targets at 40 TPS sustained, we probably need a pool with H100 as the primary option unless we shard aggressively and accept more instances.
- Concurrency behavior: given chatty sessions, we should optimize for high concurrent sessions with small per-call tokens. Recommend including a continuous-batching profile and a KV-cache sizing row in the workbook (affects memory more than GPU count).
- Burst strategy: show a baseline reserved commit sized for sustained 40 TPS and a burst reserve that adds capacity for 120 TPS spikes (preemptible or burstable hours) — call out cost delta.
- Network: include RTT assumptions for us-east <-> us-west if they want cross-region failover.

I’ll take the H100 workbook tab and sketch the instance mix; Priyom you can model the cost lines / commit tiers.

Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Solutions | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

> On Sat, Jan 23, 2027 at 14:55 Marta Gomez <marta.gomez@acadiahealth.com> wrote:

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Gomez <marta.gomez@acadiahealth.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acadiahealth.com
Date: Sat, 23 Jan 2027 16:00:00 -0800
Subject: Re: AcadiaHealth deployment follow-up — sizing clarifications & next steps

Marta / team — quick confirmation from procurement side and next steps: 

1) We received the sample template — thanks in advance for the export. Once we ingest the CSV we will:
   - run a token-distribution analysis (breakout: prompt vs completion tokens, 95th token length)
   - produce two capacity scenarios: (A) Dedicated H100 primary with A100 canary; (B) Dedicated A100 primary + more nodes.
2) For cost transparency we’ll include monthly commit tiers (reserved), burst credits, and the expected overage rates for sustained spikes.
3) If you prefer Private VPC later, we’ll flag the networking checklist now to avoid surprises (VPC peering, egress rules, HSM/KMS key options).

Action items for Monday
- Acadia: upload token samples + any peak-day event notes (Marta).
- Redwood: deliver capacity workbook (H100/A100 tabs), a short ops checklist for Dedicated vs Private VPC, and a proposed canary plan.

I’ll schedule a 45-minute sizing review for Tuesday 10:00am PT (tentative) — please reply if that conflicts.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.ai

Attachments included by Redwood: acadia_capacity_workbook.xlsx (capacity tabs: H100 / A100 / burst-policy)
